CERRITOS FINE ARTS AND HISTORICAL COMMISSION
THURSDAY - MAY 16, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the City Manager's Office, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 3rd floor, Cerritos, CA, 90703 during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the Commission after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection at the City Manager's Office during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to FineArts@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1311 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to FineArts@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the City Manager's Office no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the Commission prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  CERRITOS FINE ARTS AND HISTORICAL COMMISSION HELD
  May 16, 2024

Regular Fine Arts and Historical Commission Meeting
May 16, 2024
City Council Chambers
Bloomfield Avenue at 183rd Street
Cerritos, California 90703

PRESENT:  Commissioner Kelly Colwell
  Commissioner Michelle H. Guerrero
  Commissioner Matthew S. Kauble
  Vice Chair C.J. Villaluna
  Chair Parimal Shah

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Shah called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. in the Cerritos City Council
  Chambers, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, California.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Chair Shah.

3.  ROLL CALL

  All Members of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission were present.

4.  PUBLIC COMMENTS AND SUGGESTIONS

  Chair Shah invited public comments.

  There were no public comments and Chair Shah closed this portion of the meeting.

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  MOTION: Commissioner Kauble moved to approve the minutes of the regular
  meeting of March 21, 2024, 7:00 p.m., as presented. Commissioner Guerrero
  seconded the motion, which carried, 5-0, by roll call vote.

6.  NEW AND OLD BUSINESS

6A.  Annual Reorganization of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto declared the positions of Chair and Vice Chair of
  the Commission, vacant, and called for nominations.

  Commissioner Kauble nominated Commissioner C.J. Villaluna for Chair.

  There were no other nominations and nominations were closed.
   Commissioner C.J. Villaluna was declared Chair, unanimously, and took her place on
  the dais.

  Chair Villaluna called for nominations for Vice Chair.

  Commissioner Kauble nominated Commissioner Colwell for Vice Chair.

  There were no other nominations and nominations were closed.

  Commissioner Colwell was declared Vice Chair, unanimously and took her place on
  the dais.

6B.  Review and Consideration of a Potential Request for City Council Approval to
  Conduct a Community Survey for the Selection of a Cow-Themed Art Piece.

  Review and Consideration of Concepts for a Public Art Piece Generally
  Described as the Cerritos Cow to Represent the City’s History.

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto presented details of the report.

  Discussion followed regarding options for actions by the FAHC, estimated survey
  costs and timelines, choosing from the three concepts that were previously
  presented and avoiding further delays in the project.

  MOTION: Vice Chair Colwell moved to move forward and review the three cow-
  themed concepts submitted by Jane DeDecker, Daniel Glanz and Cammie and
  George Lundeen that were previously presented rather than proceed with a
  community survey. Commissioner Kauble seconded the motion.

  Discussion followed regarding City Council being the final approving authority.

  The motion, which carried 5-0, by roll call vote.

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto reviewed details of each concept for the FAHC’s
  consideration and reported a location will be determined at a later date.

  Discussion followed regarding prices being subject to change due to increased
  material, labor, transportation and installation costs, adding colored patina, the
  balance of the Art In Public Places Fund, expected future contributions to the fund,
  the possibility of adding/removing pieces, maintenance and potential timelines to
  produce each piece.

  Members of the FAHC shared their preferences for the project.

  MOTION: Chair Villaluna moved to recommend to City Council, approval of “Milking
  Time” by Jane DeDecker with colored patina for a public art piece generally described
  as the Cerritos cow to represent the City’s history. Vice Chair Colwell seconded the
  motion, which carried, 4-1, by roll call vote, with Commissioner Kauble, opposed.

 6C.  Status Report for Public Art Projects

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto provided a status report of public art projects;
  discussed the City website update and addressed the history component of the
  website.

  Discussion followed regarding the timeline for the rollout of the City website updates.

7.  COMMUNICATIONS

7A.  Reports from the Fine Arts and Historical Commissioners - None

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:07 p.m.

  /s/Kathleen J. Matsumoto
